clue.text: A Sitwell in Brest relaxing after round

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so the letters of the port's name drop out of their rigid order

blocks.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
the French port, taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A member of a literary family takes it easy in a Breton port after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after round' puts the O first. The Sitwells were a famous English literary trio: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Osbert Sitwell was one of the three writing siblings of the Sitwell family, so he is literally a Sitwell.

clue.text: Film from the novel Rocket Boys

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the title's letters are given a new arrangement

blocks.note: the book title, taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A trivia question asking which movie was adapted from Homer Hickam's memoir Rocket Boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like it names the book's genre, but it signals the rearrangement. The neat trick is that the real 1999 film of that memoir has an anagram of its source as its title.
explanation.definitionFit: October Sky is a 1999 Hollywood movie, adapted from Homer Hickam's memoir Rocket Boys.

clue.text: Opening claret first ahead of start of season's hunting?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept from the next word

blocks.note: claret is old boxing slang for blood, from its red colour
the first letter of season's
a port is an opening, as in a porthole or an inlet

explanation.surface: Uncorking the claret before the start of the hunting season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' moves the claret piece to the front, and the S comes ahead of the opening. The question mark flags hunting as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood sport is any sport involving killing animals, and hunting is the prime example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Copy agent runs off initially

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letter of the preceding word is used

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
the first letter of off

explanation.surface: A spy or salesman makes a copy of something and dashes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy of an original such as furniture or a painting.

clue.text: Argues with husband and son about a weapon

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters wrap round what follows

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
taken as written
a sword is a bladed weapon
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family row in which father and son fight over a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Husband and son together make the outer pair, round A SWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words with someone is the idiom for quarrelling with them, so has words means argues.

clue.text: Farcical NHS drama, meant as a comedy?

indicators.note: something farcical is absurdly chaotic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A hospital television drama so ridiculous it might as well have been written as a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, the setting of many TV hospital dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms and the Man is a comic play by George Bernard Shaw; the question mark marks it as one example of a comedy.

clue.text: Item of furniture in annexe, one covered by cleaner

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a wing is an annexe extending a building
the Roman numeral for one
a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture stored in an annexe has a dust sheet put over it by the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: Char, short for charwoman, is a British word for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing chair is an armchair with side panels projecting from its high back, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Hera's fabulous mother

indicators.note: fabulous means belonging to fable, so the goddess's name is made up into a new form

blocks.note: the goddess's name, taken as written for rearranging

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: in Greek myth, a fable in itself, Hera's mother was a Titaness whose name rearranges Hera's.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the Titan Rhea bore Hera, Zeus and their siblings to Cronus.

clue.text: Bullet's from captain's Luger

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, which hold them in sequence

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bullet has been fired from an army captain's German pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: A Luger is a German pistol, which keeps the solver thinking of ammunition while the answer sits inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Slug is informal for a bullet, especially a large or misshapen one.

clue.text: Pair of scarlet women

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters are drawn from inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A couple of women of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: A scarlet woman is an old phrase for a promiscuous woman, which pulls the solver toward a pair of hussies.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of exactly two, so the number stands in for it.

clue.text: Left gown in travelling bag

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
a manteau is a loose gown or cloak once worn by women

explanation.surface: Someone left a gown packed in their suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as the verb abandoned but is the nautical word for that side.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling case opening into two halves, so it is a bag for journeys.

clue.text: It enables one to see the other side without changing one's position

definitions.text: It enables one to see the other side without changing one's position

blocks.clueFragment: It enables one to see the other side without changing one's position
blocks.note: surface reading: something like a mirror or a philosophy that lets you see the opposing argument without giving up your own stance
setter's reading: the other side is the other television channel, and changing position means getting up from the sofa

explanation.walkthrough: 'The other side' was the old British slang for the other TV channel, when there were only two or three; the device lets you switch without leaving your seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset that switches television channels from a distance lets the viewer stay seated while changing what is on screen.

clue.text: Boredom dispelled - ticket price includes opening of Coward play

indicators.note: dispelled means driven off and scattered, so the letters are broken up and reordered
the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is used
includes means takes inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
a fare is the price of a ticket to travel
the first letter of Coward

explanation.surface: A bored theatregoer cheers up when the ticket price covers the opening night of a Noël Coward comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside FARE. 'Coward play' looks like the definition, but the playwright only gives a letter; this play is by Alan Ayckbourn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedroom Farce is a 1975 comedy by Alan Ayckbourn, so it is a play.

clue.text: Check bar turn

blocks.note: a counter is the bar across which drinks or goods are served
an act is a turn, a performer's spot in a show

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a bar act's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To counteract is to act against something and so to hold it in check or neutralise it.

clue.text: Dig down by station

blocks.note: under means down below, as in going under
a stand is a station, a place where one is posted

explanation.surface: An order to excavate beside a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like a spade instruction, but it is the slang verb for grasping something.
explanation.definitionFit: Dig is informal for grasp or appreciate, as in 'you dig?', which is to comprehend.

clue.text: Produced a further edition in red - Pinter staggered

indicators.note: staggered means reeled about unsteadily, so the letters lurch out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: The playwright Harold Pinter was astonished to see a new edition of his work printed in red ink.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprint a book is to print it again, issuing another edition.

clue.text: Popular French novelist's introduction to sedate Scottish city

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
Jules Verne, the French author of science fiction, with the possessive 's
the first letter of sedate

explanation.surface: A well-liked French writer's opening to a calm Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on 'novelist's' is not padding: it supplies the first of the two final S's.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is a city in the Scottish Highlands, at the mouth of the River Ness.

clue.text: Goodness in an oak's fruit

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, which wraps around it

blocks.note: taken as written
Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like Goodness!

explanation.surface: Praise for the nutritional goodness of the nut on an oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: COR goes between A and N. Cor is everyday British slang for an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut that an oak tree bears, its seed-bearing fruit.

clue.text: Irish in knockout victory in Russian city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another that wraps around it

blocks.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in the V sign

explanation.surface: An Irish boxer wins by a knockout in a Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is doing double duty in the surface as the location of the fight, but here it places Irish inside knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirov is a city in western Russia, formerly and now again called Vyatka.

clue.text: Sticking together in creche one built

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are assembled into a new structure

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Children at a nursery stick together while making something.
explanation.walkthrough: A creche is a nursery for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is the quality of things cohering, holding together as a unified whole.

clue.text: How to describe concert pianists, exceptionally skilful players?

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: masters of the concert grand piano
second meaning: chess players holding the highest title

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word in two: concert pianists play a grand, so they are masters of it. The second is the chess title.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmaster is a chess player of the highest rank, and concert pianists are masters of the grand piano.

clue.text: A term for an Englishman in India has upset one bishop

definitions.text: A term for an Englishman in India

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: An Englishman in the Raj is offended by a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib, meaning master, was the respectful form of address for European men in colonial India.

clue.text: Painter, Ray, ultimately shown in part of India

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is kept
shown in means put on display inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
the last letter of Ray

explanation.surface: An exhibition of a painter called Ray is finally put on in a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a painter's first name but supplies only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Travel document is required to enter Virginia

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller is told what paperwork is needed to enter the state of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes between V and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement in a passport allowing entry to a country, a document for travelling.

clue.text: Offer of reconciliation made by girl on section

blocks.note: Olive is a girl's name
a branch is a section or division of an organisation

explanation.surface: A young woman working in one department makes a peace offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the girl before the section.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding out an olive branch is the idiom for offering peace, from the dove's olive leaf in the Noah story.

clue.text: Commander heading for Augusta, Georgia

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the first letter of the city name is used

blocks.note: the first letter of Augusta
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A military commander is travelling to Augusta in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusta really is a city in Georgia, which makes 'heading for' read as travel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Water, alas, made impure

indicators.note: something impure has been adulterated, so these letters are spoiled into a new mix

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A lament that the drinking water has been polluted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' looks like part of the surface verb but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular name for plain water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: Sailor, on special date, calmed down

indicators.note: special suggests something specially arranged, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A sailor on a special date settles his nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the sailor before the rearranged date.
explanation.definitionFit: Abated means lessened or subsided, as a storm or anger does when it calms.
